clue.text: Is neat rum a healthy thing to drink?

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters before it are to be put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether neat rum counts as a health drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being described, but it is the adjective meaning odd: rearrange ISNEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a caffeine-free drink taken for its supposed health benefits.

clue.text: Old radio part editor changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word before it are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor has swapped out a component in a vintage wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-electrode valve was a standard component of early radio sets before transistors.

clue.text: Such characters are simply executed

parts.note: characters here are printed letters, and simply executed means drawn plainly without the little finishing strokes at their ends

explanation.surface: It sounds like people being put to death without ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface style whose letters lack the small cross-strokes at the ends of their lines, making them plain.

clue.text: Choice of courses for old sea-raiders

parts.note: a course is a compass direction; north is N
a choice between alternatives is expressed by or
a second compass course, south-east, is SE

explanation.surface: A menu offering a selection of dishes for some ancient seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests a meal, but these are compass bearings: N, then OR for 'Choice', then SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings who raided by sea came from Scandinavia, and Norse names those people.

clue.text: A friend 'with short dress in Gulf port

parts.note: bud is an American informal word for a friend, short for buddy

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a habit is a garment, especially a monk's or nun's dress

explanation.surface: A companion in a skimpy outfit turns up in a harbour on the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims HABIT to HABI.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the United Arab Emirates is a city and harbour on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: This port can make one cheerful, so they say

indicators.note: so they say tells us the word is something heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: blithe means cheerful and carefree

explanation.surface: A seaside town whose name supposedly lifts the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: BLYTH is a port in Northumberland, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town on the Northumberland coast of England, an example of a port.

clue.text: Daughter joins exclusive clique of dishy things?

parts.note: an inner set is a select group admitted to the centre of things

explanation.surface: A girl breaks into a select social circle of attractive people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishy' looks like attractive, but the definition means things made of dishes, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching collection of plates and bowls for a meal is a group of crockery items.

clue.text: A dessert that must be served up cold

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a fool is a British pudding of puréed fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A pudding that has to be brought to the table chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' seems to describe the dessert but is the definition, meaning distant in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cold in manner is distant and reserved, keeping apart from others.

clue.text: How class thinks I had to replace head of science

indicators.note: to replace head of says the first letter of the next word is swapped out for what came before

parts.note: geology is the science of rocks and the earth
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A Marxist explanation of class consciousness replacing a scientist in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The G at the head of GEOLOGY gives way to ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of beliefs held by a social class, as in Marxist theory, shapes its thinking.

clue.text: Girl mostly appearing like this, in pink, say

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Diana is a girl's name
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A girl turns up dressed this way in pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' looks like a colour, but here it is the garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks and carnations belong to this plant genus, so a pink is an example.

clue.text: Change to noon first time of express for central Manchester, say

indicators.note: Change to says one letter is swapped for another, here the first T giving way

parts.note: InterCity was the British Rail brand for fast express trains

explanation.surface: Timetable advice to switch to the midday express to reach Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says the first T of INTERCITY is the one changed.
explanation.definitionFit: The densely built central district of a big city, often rundown, is called by this name.

clue.text: She was all tears in returning honour

indicators.note: returning means the little word before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone weeps on coming back with a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children; 'all tears' is Hamlet's phrase for her.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical mother who, turned to stone, wept forever for her lost children.

clue.text: Clearly see record has merit, listening to it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: listening to it says the word is as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A critic finds a record worthwhile once they hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive something distinctly, to make it out, is to see it clearly.

clue.text: Taking care of male editor with nasty flu

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word after it is in a bad way, so jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a sick male editor with a bad dose of flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns FLU into FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mindful and attentive, paying attention, is being careful.

clue.text: Something saucy that mightn't be seen at the Folies-Bergeres?

definitions.text: Something saucy that mightn't be seen at the Folies-Bergeres?

parts.words: Something saucy that mightn't be seen at the Folies-Bergeres?
parts.note: saucy means a sauce for salad, and the Paris cabaret is famed for undressed dancers, so clothing is the thing missing there

explanation.surface: A risqué show in Paris where clothing is in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The Folies-Bergère is a Paris music hall famous for nearly nude showgirls.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette is the oil-and-vinegar salad sauce known by this name.

clue.text: Special coinage that's new, as soon as command is given

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, as in once you arrive
a word is an order, as in give the word

explanation.surface: Fresh money is minted the moment the order goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' suggests money but means a newly invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: A term invented for one particular occasion is a one-off invented expression.

clue.text: Go to country, possibly Israel, after game

indicators.note: after says the rearranged word follows the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: possibly says the word before it may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to the countryside, perhaps Israel, once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns ISRAEL into ALISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or become rustic, adopting a country way of life.

clue.text: I agree nothing awfully sour could be free from smell

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement
O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: awfully says the word after it is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that nothing so sour could be odourless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns SOUR into ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any odour, so having no scent at all.

clue.text: Having potential for learning, possible due to one sort of TV

indicators.note: possible hints at a possible arrangement of the following word's letters

parts.note: cable is one kind of television service

explanation.surface: A student's promise might owe something to the kind of television they watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' turns DUE into EDU.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being taught, so able to be schooled.

clue.text: Expulsion from Oriel, say

parts.note: Oriel looks like the Oxford college, but an oriel is a projecting window, and being thrown out of one is the act described

explanation.surface: A student is sent down from an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing someone out through a window is the act this word names.

clue.text: Complaint made by crazy eccentric about nothing

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the word before it is put in odd order

parts.note: O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: An odd grievance raised by a crazy oddball over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' gives CRYZA from CRAZY; 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold is a minor ailment, and complaint is an old word for an illness.

clue.text: Flier gets water from French in one of their big houses

parts.note: a chat is a small songbird, so a flier
eau is the French word for water

explanation.surface: A bird drinks French water in a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand country house or castle in France.

clue.text: Speak without preparation of publicity by old party

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is publicity
the Liberals, Lib, were the old British party before merging into the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A party spokesperson improvises some publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise, saying something off the cuff without a script.

clue.text: Release capital from the BBC

indicators.note: capital from says the capital, the first letter, is taken off the nickname that follows

parts.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: Funding being released from the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a knot or tied thing is to set it free.

clue.text: African river father's entered in luxurious transport

indicators.note: entered in means put inside the word that follows

parts.note: a limo, limousine, is luxurious transport
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad has climbed into a limousine somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A major southern African waterway flowing into the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Female artist supporting me in Paris

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: moi is French for me
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman painter backs someone in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so it serves as an example of a female.

clue.text: Blade cutting first William, then Robert

indicators.note: cutting means the names lose their final letters

parts.note: Bill is a pet form of William
Bob is a pet form of Robert

explanation.surface: A knife attacks William and then Robert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' trims both names, BILL to BIL and BOB to BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilbo is an old kind of sword, named after Bilbao in Spain.

clue.text: Witness is cross about one at start of week

indicators.note: about means wrapped around what follows

parts.note: testy means irritable, cross
I is the Roman numeral for one
Mon, Monday, is the start of the week

explanation.surface: A witness gets annoyed about one appearance early in the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence given in court is what a witness provides.

clue.text: Made material, old and faded, to put on English doctor

indicators.note: to put on says these pieces are attached after the earlier ones

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
died means faded away

explanation.surface: Old, faded fabric is draped over an English doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made material' looks like fabric making, but means given bodily form.
explanation.definitionFit: Given physical form, made concrete or incarnate.

clue.text: Some in China use acupuncture for this sickness

indicators.note: Some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In China acupuncture is a remedy for feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy, wanting to vomit, is a kind of sickness.
